newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin approves Russia-Belarus draft accord-Tass.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin approves Russia-Belarus draft accord-Tass.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin approved on Monday a draft accord on forming a union between Russia and Belarus, a Kremlin aide told Itar-Tass news agency.

Yeltsin's top foreign affairs adviser, Dmitry Ryurikov, told Tass the Kremlin leader had given the green light to the accord, which is due to be signed on Wednesday with Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko.
The Kremlin press service could not immediately confirm the Tass report. Earlier it had said Yeltsin was reviewing the document at his country residence.

The text of the document has not been published. But a draft obtained by Reuters on Monday provided for a union under which the two states would remain independent but coordinate their foreign, economic and military policies closely.

Kremlin sources said liberals in the government had mounted a rearguard action to prevent Yeltsin signing the document, which they fear could allow the hardline Lukashenko to gain a slice of power in Russia.
Russian liberals are also concerned by the economic implications of integration with the smaller and less wealthy state of about 10 million people where economic reforms have made less headway.
